product_brief: Secure IoT and cybersecurity-focused satellite constellation enabling quantum-safe key distribution and device onboarding.
pqc_capability_description: The constellation aims to support quantum-safe key distribution and secure IoT device onboarding from orbit starting in early 2026. It is designed to integrate seamlessly with SEALSQ post-quantum chips. It delivers quantum-resistant digital identities from orbit.
target_industries: Government, defense, enterprise, energy, transportation, smart cities, industrial IoT, environmental monitoring, critical-infrastructure protection
pqc_roadmap_details: Beginning with its next launch planned for early 2026, the constellation will support quantum-safe key distribution for critical infrastructure sectors.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for secure IoT device onboarding, low-power IoT services, and extending trusted connectivity to remote or underserved areas.

product_brief: Industry’s first scalable symmetric key distribution technology achieving future-proofed security without asymmetric encryption.
pqc_capability_description: DSKE delivers future-proofed security at scale without the use of any asymmetric cryptography. It integrates seamlessly with existing systems and encryption protocols, including Post-Quantum Cryptography and Quantum Key Distribution Systems. It ensures secure symmetric key distribution with protection against both quantum and classical attacks.
crypto_primitives: Symmetric cryptographic algorithms (generic), Pre-shared random data (PSRD), Secret sharing algorithm. No specific asymmetric primitives (e.g., RSA, ECDSA) are stated as being used by DSKE itself; it operates without them.
key_management_model: Distributed Symmetric Key Establishment (DSKE) using pre-shared random numbers (PSRD) between clients and Security Hubs. Uses a secret sharing scheme to allow key creation without trusting individual Security Hubs. Keys are rebuilt by clients only.
architecture_type: Security hubs and DSKE clients over IP networks.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: Integrates with Quantum Key Distribution Systems. Specific protocols (BB84, etc.) not stated.
qrng_&_entropy_sources: Uses high quality random numbers, also called pre-shared random data (PSRD). Specific source type or NIST compliance not stated.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Integrates seamlessly with existing systems and encryption protocols.

product_brief: Purpose-built key management platform that neutralizes HNDL attacks and adapts to evolving cryptography without downtime.
pqc_capability_description: Supports PQC through unified policy control. Crypto-agile and not algorithm-dependent. Built for multiple rounds of PQC evolution, allowing quick adoption of new NIST standards without application rewrites.
key_management_model: Out-of-band key management; separates key delivery from data transmission; centralized policy control; overlays existing infrastructure.
architecture_type: Virtual container (Phio TX-EM), Cloud deployment (Phio TX-C), Datacenter-ready appliance (Phio TX Appliance)
primary_platforms: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Virtual container, Datacenter appliance
pqc_roadmap_details: Built for multiple rounds of PQC evolution; adopts new standards quickly as NIST evaluates additional algorithms.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: Supports QKD; overlays ETSI GS QKD 014 supported infrastructure.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Deploy in days; overlays existing infrastructure; zero downtime; zero added latency; no infrastructure overhaul required.

product_brief: A research and simulation platform for Quantum Key Distribution, built as an NS-3 module.
pqc_capability_description: The document does not mention Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). It focuses on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) simulation and classical cryptographic algorithms like AES and OTP.
crypto_primitives: One-Time Pad (OTP), Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), VMAC
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: ETSI QKD compliance (referenced via test script `qkd_etsi_014.cc`)
deployment_&_migration_complexity: QKDNetSim v2.0 module is not compatible with QKDNetSim version 1.0; written independently and from scratch.

product_brief: A quantum toolbox for simulating quantum networks, entanglement routing, and teleportation protocols.
pqc_capability_description: The document describes a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and quantum network simulation software. It does not mention Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms (e.g., CRYSTALS-Kyber, Dilithium) or classical cryptographic migration. It focuses on quantum entanglement, teleportation, and quantum node simulation.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: Supports entanglement generation, purification, teleportation, and distributed entanglement routing. Simulates quantum nodes, optical channels, and noise (depolarizing/measurement error).
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Open source (GitHub), uses uv for package management, migrated from setup.py to pyproject.toml.

product_brief: Reference implementation of a 4-layer Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) network solution with key management.
pqc_capability_description: The document describes a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) network solution. It does not mention Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms, migration, or support.
key_management_model: Microservice-based Key Management System (KMS) with Configuration, Registration, Authorization, KMS Service, API Gateway, and QNL services.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: 4-layer QKD network solution (KMS, QNL, QLL, User Layer). Mentions ETSI and ITU-T standards for interfaces. Includes QLL simulator for satellite-based links.
